title: Low-power ascension (OpenMC core 242)
brief: Start from shutdown with the source in the core. Withdraw the rods to raise the power to about a tenth of the power-high trip setpoint, then hold it there for two minutes. Watch the period while the power rises and do not trip the reactor. This is the supported lesson of the OpenMC TRIGA library: steady operation up to 15 % of the trip setpoint. The banner at the top of each window says when the state leaves what the model is meant for.

envelope.summary: Steady, low-power ascension and hold, from shutdown to 15 % of the power-high setpoint; no pulses, no long runs.

power.source: the lesson's goals end at 15 % of the setpoint (docs/validation/supported-envelope.md)

fuelTemp.source: libraries/triga-jsi-242-openmc/manifest.json domain.jointChecked: the warmest checked state is 569.8 K

knownLimits.text: Measured against a real JSI power ascension, this model's power defect is only about 0.35 to 0.45 of the real value (about 650 against 1427 pcm at 250 kW), because its fuel heats too little and in proportion to power. The regulating rod needs far less withdrawal to hold a given power than in the real reactor.
knownLimits.source: docs/validation/m7-power-ascension-results.md (metric A fails for both OpenMC cores)

goals.text: Raise the power above 1 % of the power-high setpoint
Raise the power above 10 % of the power-high setpoint
Hold the power between 5 % and 12 % of the power-high setpoint for 2 minutes

hints: Withdraw the large rods first, then use the regulating rod for fine control.
A short period means the power rises fast. The period-short trip acts below 3 s.
Fuel temperature feedback slows the rise as the fuel heats up.
